display.purpose: The day's game on the oversized dashboard plate. Fredoka, capped at 600. One per screen.

headline.purpose: Play title and the game-over verdict on a stage veil.

numeral-wide.purpose: The streak count on the dashboard.

numeral-small.purpose: Number-pad digits and fixed readout figures.

stage-title.purpose: Game name in the stage bar; deliberately smaller than the dashboard display.

wordmark.purpose: The rail mark only. Fredoka 500, mixed case, near-neutral tracking.

title.purpose: Game names on slot plates and ladder names.

chalk.purpose: The annotation voice: one-liners, notes, empty-state explanation. 46-62ch measure.

label.purpose: Zone labels: the body face uppercased and tracked via --font-label.

micro.purpose: Tags, table headers, foot, peg options, key faces, tools.

nano.purpose: Readout labels, field labels, room-code label, divider rules.

cell.purpose: Sudoku digits sized in cqmin against the board's own container.

shadows.name: lift-1
shadows.purpose: Resting elevation: plates, nameplate, room-code fitting. Day coat rebuilds it from navy mixes.

shadows.name: lift-2
shadows.purpose: A whole game surface: sudoku board, play surface, legacy panel.

shadows.name: cut
shadows.purpose: Every routed channel: slot, readout, status, field, peg groove.

shadows.name: key-rest
shadows.purpose: The primary key at rest; 4px on hover, 1px on active.

shadows.name: rail-seat
shadows.purpose: The sticky rail seated on the board.

motion.name: swing
motion.purpose: The board's easing: plate drops, key presses, peg slides.

motion.name: hang-drop
motion.purpose: A plate landing on its hook. Under review; do not extend to new surfaces.

motion.name: hang-lift
motion.purpose: The outgoing plate leaving the hook; the replacement waits 200ms for the hook to clear.

motion.name: draw-mark
motion.value: 340ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) dash reveal; strike 420ms with 160ms delay
motion.purpose: Stroked SVG marks drawing themselves in. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: state-fade
motion.purpose: Color and border transitions on controls.

components.name: BrainBox Mark
components.description: A solid brain. Two mirrored halves of one silhouette filled in the signal paint, with the hemisphere division and four folds cut out of the fill by a mask so the ground shows through and the mark needs no second colour.
components.html: BrainBox
components.css: .ds-mark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; color: var(--ink, #e8edf4); } .ds-mark svg { flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-mark-word { font-family: var(--font-display), sans-serif; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.005em; font-size: clamp(1.3rem, 2.3vw, 1.6rem); line-height: 1; }

components.name: Key (primary action)
components.description: The primary action, built as a pressed fitting rather than a button.

components.name: Key Quiet (secondary action)
components.description: The secondary action: a keyline outline that goes cobalt on hover and never moves.
components.css: .ds-key-quiet { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; padding: 14px 26px; background: transparent; color: var(--ink-quiet, #b3bfd0); border: 1px solid var(--keyline-strong, rgba(232,237,244,0.32)); border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 12px); font-family: var(--font-label, var(--font-text)), sans-serif; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; font-size: 0.82rem; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; transition: color 140ms ease-out, border-color 140ms ease-out; } .ds-key-quiet:hover { color: var(--ink, #e8edf4); border-color: var(--signal, #4f8ce8); } .ds-key-quiet:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal, #4f8ce8); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Plate
components.description: The raised enamel container every figure sits on: dark border, concentric inset keyline, hard offset shadow.

components.name: Slot (routed channel)
components.description: The cut container: everything recessed is this channel plus the inset cut shadow, at the softest corner on the scale.
components.css: .ds-slot { background: var(--routed, #050a11); border-radius: var(--radius-lg, 20px); box-shadow: inset 0 3px 7px rgba(0,0,0,0.62), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(232,237,244,0.07); padding: 16px; } .ds-slot-label { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-label, var(--font-text)), sans-serif; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.12em; font-size: 0.72rem; color: var(--ink-quiet, #b3bfd0); }

components.css: .ds-readout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0,1fr)); background: var(--routed, #050a11); border-radius: var(--radius-lg, 20px); box-shadow: inset 0 3px 7px rgba(0,0,0,0.62), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(232,237,244,0.07); overflow: hidden; } .ds-readout-item { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; padding: 12px 14px; border-right: 1px solid var(--keyline, rgba(232,237,244,0.16)); } .ds-readout-item:last-child { border-right: 0; } .ds-readout-label { font-family: var(--font-label, var(--font-text)), sans-serif; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.13em; font-size: 0.56rem; color: var(--ink-faint, #8b98a9); } .ds-readout-value { font-family: var(--font-display), sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 1.5rem; line-height: 1; color: var(--ink, #e8edf4); } .ds-readout-value.ds-is-warn { color: var(--signal-ink, #5f95e6); }

components.name: Rail Navigation

narrative.overview:
BrainBox is a hand-operated board in a club back room, painted in navy and cobalt. Nothing on it is generated: every figure sits on an enamel plate that somebody screwed to a hook, every region is a channel routed into the panel, every label is painted on. The interface reads as fabricated hardware rather than rendered software.

The hardware is rounded, not machined. Corners run on a soft scale (8/12/16/20px), the display face is curvy and capped at semibold, and the mark is a solid brain with its folds cut out. The board is friendly and it does not shout — the tone commitment is carried by the corner scale and the weight ceiling, not by adding color.

The board is lit two ways. The night coat is the navy ground with bone ink; the day coat relights the same board without touching the paint tin — roles swap, paints do not. There are five paints and no sixth. Every tone between them is a color-mix of two paints, never a new pigment and never a gradient.

Density is high but the voice is warm. Numbers are large, rounded and tabular; supporting text is small, quiet and short. Game play takes the whole window: a route that plays something claims the full viewport below the rail and sizes its board to that space rather than growing the page. Confirmed rejection: no gradients, no soft glassy translucency as a surface, no decorative color that is not also a fitting.
keyCharacteristics: Five paints, closed; every other tone is a mix of two of them
Two coats that swap roles, not paints (night is default; day is a relight)
One rounded corner scale (8/12/16/20/999px); nothing gets a bespoke radius
Two faces, two-and-a-half roles: Fredoka is the voice, Nunito is the reading and, set in caps and tracked, the labels
Display weight is capped at 600 — the board never shouts
Depth is offset-plus-blur shadow standing off the board, or an inset routed channel cut into it — never both directions in one element
A single fixed speckle layer over the whole window; no per-element texture
State is a written word plus a drawn mark, never color alone
Play routes own the window: a fixed-height stage, a board that fits it

rules.name: The Five Paints Rule
rules.body: The palette is closed at five: navy, slate, steel, bone, cobalt. Any new tone is a color-mix of two of them. A sixth pigment requires a palette decision, not a component decision. Fault red is the single documented exception and is reserved for error.

rules.name: The Repaint Rule
rules.body: The day coat swaps roles, not paints. [data-paint="day"] reassigns --ground, --ink, --signal, --signal-on, --panel, --routed and the shadow tokens; it never introduces a hex. Audit test: if a component reads --paint-* directly for a fill or a text color, it must look right in both coats or be rewritten onto a role token. The one licensed exception is a static asset that cannot read a variable: app/icon.svg and app/apple-icon.svg hardcode navy, bone and cobalt because a favicon has no CSS context.

rules.name: The Signal Is Not Text Rule
rules.body: Cobalt at ~4.4:1 on navy is a fill, a stroke, and large display type — never body text, never a small label. Words in the accent use --signal-ink.

rules.name: The Computed Contrast Rule
rules.body: --ink-quiet, --ink-faint, --plate-ink-quiet and every keyline mix are computed to clear 4.5:1 against their own ground in both coats. Changing a mix percentage means recomputing, not eyeballing.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Fredoka and Nunito, both self-hosted through next/font, no third family and no system display stack. --font-label is an alias of --font-text, not a new face. A new weight inside the loaded set is allowed; a new family is a system change.

rules.name: The Quiet Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Display type stops at 600. No 700, 800 or 900 anywhere in the display role — the ramp gets its emphasis from size, never from mass. Nunito's 700 exists for inline body emphasis only.

rules.name: The Caps-For-Labels Rule
rules.body: The label role is the body face uppercased and tracked: zone labels, tags, button faces, column headers, unit lines. It is always uppercase, always letterspaced between 0.12em and 0.16em, and never sets a sentence.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Figures are tabular. font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on body and re-asserted on every numeral class, so a score never shifts width as it changes.

rules.name: The Every-Zone-Names-Itself Rule
rules.body: Every region of the board opens with a zone label whose trailing hairline runs to the edge of the region. Wayfinding is reading, not iconography.

rules.name: The Stage Owns The Window Rule
rules.body: A play route claims the window below the rail and nothing inside it may grow that height. Boards fit the stage; the stage never fits the board. Audit test: with the game running at 1280x800, the page must not scroll.

rules.name: The Page Owns Its Container Rule
rules.body: The layout supplies no width and no padding. Every page states its own container — .board__inner for reading surfaces, .stage for play.

rules.name: The Two Directions Rule
rules.body: Every depth effect either stands off the board (offset + blur) or is cut into it (inset). Never both on one element, and never a shadow with zero offset.

rules.name: The No-Gradient Rule
rules.body: No gradient anywhere. An apparent tone shift is a color-mix of two paints, the speckle layer, or a shadow.

rules.name: The One Speckle Rule
rules.body: One fixed speckle layer for the whole window. Components do not carry their own texture, noise, or backdrop except the stage veil's single 3px blur.

rules.name: The One Corner Scale Rule
rules.body: Every corner on the board comes from --radius-xs / -sm / --radius / -lg / -pill. No component declares its own radius literal. Audit test: a border-radius in the sheet that is not a var(--radius*) reference is a bug, with the two documented exceptions — the 12px concentric inner keyline and the 50% drilled hole in the hung plate.

rules.name: The One Stroke Rule
rules.body: Every mark on the board is drawn at one weight in one file, so hardware and game marks read as a single set of fittings. A new icon is added there or not at all.

dos: Do build from role tokens (--ground, --ink, --signal, --signal-on, --panel, --routed) so a component relights in both coats for free.
Do use --signal-ink for any word in the accent color, and reserve --signal for fills, strokes and large display type.
Do express every space as a calc(var(--u) * n) multiple of the 8px unit.
Do set labels in the body face, uppercased and tracked 0.12em-0.16em, via --font-label.
Do give each new game a .stage with a .stage__bar and a .stage__body, and assemble its side rail from the existing furniture (.readout, .pad, .tools, .status, .field, .notice).
Do size a game board to the stage — container queries or cqmin type, min-height: 0 on the grid track — so the page never scrolls during play.
Do state every status with a word plus a drawn form; color confirms it, it does not carry it.
Do draw new marks in components/board/icons.js at the 1.6 stroke weight on the 24x24 box.
Do open every region with a zone label.
Do keep the mark's interior at three strokes; it is a tested legibility floor at 16px.
donts: Don't introduce a sixth paint. New tones are color-mix of the five. Fault red is the single documented exception and is only for error.
Don't use a gradient anywhere, on any surface, in any coat.
Don't set body text, small labels or long copy in --signal.
Don't set display type above 600, and don't reach for weight where size is the correct emphasis.
Don't write a bespoke border-radius literal; if the scale is wrong, change the scale.
Don't add a second texture, noise or backdrop layer; the fixed speckle is the whole budget.
Don't let a play route's content determine the page height, and don't put a page container in the root layout.
Don't add a third font family or fall back to a system display face.
Don't ship a glyph icon, an icon font, or an icon at a stroke weight other than 1.6.
Don't redraw the mark's brain as a single continuous path (it reads as a "2") or as dense parallel folds (it fills in at 16px).
Don't extend the hung-plate mechanic to new surfaces while it is under review.
Don't treat .legacy as a component to reuse; it exists only until chess is rebuilt.
